sections.markdown:
## C — Other important information: reportable medical conditions, supervising drivers, organ donation, voter registration, insurance, seat belts, child seats and air bags

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A51
If you have a listed medical condition you must tell the MVA when you apply for or renew a license, or when the condition is diagnosed if that happens after licensing. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A51
For a listed condition that could affect driving, the MVA's Driver Wellness and Safety Division and or its Medical Advisory Board must approve you for a license. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A51
Diabetes is reportable when it caused a low blood sugar episode needing another person's help within the past 6 months. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A51
A heart condition is reportable when it caused a loss of consciousness within the past 6 months. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A51
Epilepsy or seizures, stroke, conditions causing dizzy spells, fainting or blackouts, sleep apnea or narcolepsy, and a history of traumatic brain injury are reportable. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A51
Weakness, shaking or numbness in the arms, hands, legs or feet, or a missing, amputated or impaired limb, is reportable when it may affect your driving. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A51
An eye problem is reportable if it keeps your corrected acuity from reaching at least 20/70 in one eye or your binocular field of vision from reaching 110 degrees. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A51
Alcohol or drug use problems, a mental health condition that may affect driving, schizophrenia and dementia are also reportable. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A51
A Maryland Learner's Permit holder may drive only the vehicles or vehicle class the permit names, and always with a supervising driver. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A51
A supervising driver must be at least 21 years old. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A51
A supervising driver must have held a license for at least 3 years, in Maryland or another state, for the same class of vehicle you are driving. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A51
The supervising driver must sit beside you, except when the vehicle is a motorcycle. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A51
Anyone 18 or older may become an organ donor. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A51
A minor aged at least 16 may be an organ donor with a parent's or guardian's written consent. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A52
If you agree to be a donor on your application or renewal, your license can show that you are an organ donor. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A52
The federal National Voter Registration Act of 1993, known as Motor Voter, requires the MVA to let eligible customers register to vote or update voter details when getting a license or photo ID card. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A52
Every vehicle registered in Maryland must be insured by a company licensed in Maryland. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A52
Vehicle owners must carry personal injury and property damage liability coverage in the amounts the law sets, which the MVA website lists. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A52
Always carry a valid insurance identification card when driving, which may be electronic, and show it when an officer asks or risk a fine. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A52
The law requires the driver and every passenger to wear a seat belt or be secured in a child safety seat. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A52
Every child under 8 must ride in a child safety seat unless the child is at least 4 feet 9 inches tall. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A52
A child younger than 2 must ride rear-facing in a seat meeting federal guidelines until reaching the maker's height or weight limit. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A52
Follow every instruction from your child seat's maker and your vehicle's maker; child safety seats include car seats, booster seats and other federally approved devices. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A52
Families who cannot afford a seat can contact the Maryland Department of Health's Kids In Safety Seats program, which runs low-cost car and booster seat rentals, though seats are not always available everywhere. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A52
Air bags protect best when used with the lap and shoulder belt and when you sit as far from the wheel as you can, keeping 10 to 12 inches between the wheel and your chest. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A52
A pregnant woman should wear the lap belt under the abdomen, low on the hips and across the upper thighs, with the shoulder belt over the rounding of the belly. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A52
A child in a rear-facing car seat must never ride in a front seat that has a passenger air bag. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A52
Children under 13 should sit in the back, buckled into either a child safety seat or a seat belt. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A52
Anti-lock braking systems keep the wheels from locking so you can keep control of the car. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

Glossary: supervising driver — the licensed adult who must ride beside a permit holder [A51]. Motor Voter — the federal law letting MVA customers register to vote [A52]. Liability insurance — coverage for injury and property damage you cause to others [A52]. Child safety seat — a car seat, booster seat or other federally approved child restraint [A52].
Memory aid: under two faces back, under eight rides in a seat unless tall enough, under thirteen rides in back [A52].
Misconception: a reportable condition is not only one you have when you first apply; one diagnosed later must be reported when it is diagnosed [A51].
